(BY MS. VIBHA BHARUKA - GOVERNMENT ADVOCATE)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER 01.
This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, for grant of anticipatory bail.

The applicant is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.777/2022 registered at Police Station Bhanwarkuan, District-Indore for an offence punishable under Section 420, 467, 468, 120-B of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 13(1)(A),
29(1)(A), 29(1)(B), 29(1)(C) Insecticides Act and Section 7/19(C) Fertilizer Control Act 1985 and 3/7 Essential Commodities Act.
0 2 .

As per the prosecution, a complainant was lodged by Senior Agricultural Extension Officer Kishan Kalyan Indore to the effect that co- accused Sachin Kataria, Rajendra Bithare and Rajesh Suhane are carrying on the business of illegal and fictitious Urea from their house.

On the complaint the house was searched and it was found that the accused are packaging urea of M/s Mahadhan Phosphate Private Limited, Dewas which is a local brand as urea of IFFCO company, New Delhi.

They are packing the phosphate rich organic manure Aman vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47051644/
1 of M/s Mahadhan in the bags of IFFCO company and are selling the same as original IFFCO urea through various other associates including the applicant.

On the basis of the complaint and recovery, investigation was conducted during course of which the applicant has been implicated for the present offence on the allegation that he has been selling the urea of M/s Mahadhan Phosphate Private Limited, Dewas by terming the same to be of IFFCO company.
03. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
No recovery of any urea has been made from him.
The only material on record against him is the memorandum of co-accused recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act.
There is no legal evidence to connect the applicant with the present crime.
It has not been shown that the applicant has benefited in any manner by way of his alleged act.
On such grounds prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant has been made.

04. The aforesaid prayer has been opposed by learned counsel for the respondent/State submitting that in view of the allegations levelled against the applicant and the material collected by the prosecution against him, he is not entitled for grant of benefit of anticipatory bail.
05. I have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have perused the case diary.
0 6 . The implication of the applicant appears to be on basis of memorandum of co-accused recorded under Section 27 of the Evidence Act.
No recovery of the pesticide/urea has been made from the applicant.
There is no direct material connecting the applicant to the present crime.
It has not been shown that the applicant has derived any monetary advantage from the transaction.
Thus in my opinion, in view of the material on record against the applicant, he is entitled for grant of benefit of anticipatory bail.

07. It is directed that in the event of arrest of applicant by the Arresting Officer, he shall be released on bail subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties of Rs.25,000/- each out of which one shall be local surety with of like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer (Investigating Officer).
08.
The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a Police Officer, as and when required.
Applicant shall further abide by the other conditions enumerated in Sub Section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
09. This order shall be subject to the condition that the applicant shall appear before the trial Court on the next date fixed before it and shall furnish his bail bonds.
10. Accordingly, Miscellaneous Criminal Case No.31387 of 2023 stands allowed and disposed off.
Certified copy as per rules.
(PRANAY VERMA) JUDGE Shilpa Aman vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47051644/
